item.purpose: Outline the plaintiffs' initial contention regarding the applicability of the U.P. Agriculturists' Relief Act based on Sita Ram's tax status.

item.attribution: Plaintiffs' Written Statement / High Court record
item.limit: Represents a party position, not a judicial finding.

resolved_originals.text: It appears from the judgment of the High Court under'appeal that in their written statement the mortgagors claimed the benefit of the U.P. Agriculturists' Relief Act (No. XXVII of 1934). The plaintiffs contended that the mortgagors were members of a joint Hindu family and as Sita Ram one of the mortgagors was assessed to income-tax the mortgagors were not agriculturists as defined in cite17†section 2 (2) of that Act and, therefore, could not claim the benefit conferred on the agriculturists by that Act.

item.purpose: Record the Trial Court's finding on the 'agriculturist' status of Sita Ram and the other mortgagors under the 1934 Act.
item.relation_question: How did the Trial Court resolve the dispute over whether Sita Ram was an agriculturist given his income-tax assessment?
item.limit: This finding relates to the 1934 Act and the 1939 decree, distinct from the later 1940 Act proceedings.

resolved_originals.text: The trial Court, by its judgment dated March 31, 1939, held that though Sita Ram was assessed to incometax for the year 1931-32, the amount of such in- cometax did not exceed the amount of cess payable on the land held by him and consequently the second proviso to cite17†section 2 (2) did not apply to him and he was, therefore, an agriculturist and as the other mortgagors were also agricul- turists all of them were entitled to the benefits under the Act.

item.purpose: Summarize the evidence presented regarding Sita Ram's income-tax status and salary during the relevant period (1930-1932).
item.relation_question: What testimony and documentary evidence was adduced concerning Sita Ram's employment and tax liability around the time of the 1931 mortgage?
item.attribution: Witness Testimony (Sita Ram, Suraj Mani Tripathi) / Exhibit (Income-tax form)
item.limit: Evidence shows no tax deduction in 1931; assessment form dated Feb 1933 covers year 1931-32.

resolved_originals.text: Sita Ram stated that since 1907 he had been a teacher in Harish Chandra Intermediate College of Banaras, that in 1930 his salary was Rs. 90 per month, that since February 1932 to 1936 he paid incometax and that after that he paid no in- come-tax.

His evidence was corroborated by Suraj Mani Tripathi who was the Accountant of the College from 1930 to 1042. Referring to the College Acquittance Roll Suraj Mani Tripathi deposed that the pay of Sita Ram was Rs. 90 per month throughout 1930, that in 1930 no income-tax was levied, that in 1931 also his salary was Rs. 90 per month and that no income-tax was deducted in 1931 too, that the first deduction of in- come-tax from his salary was made in February 1932.

No rebutting evidence was adduced by the decree-holders on the hearing of the application under cite14†section 8 of the Act of 1940. The income-tax assessment form filed during the trial of the mortgage suit and marked as exhibits is dated Febru- ary 9, 1933, and shows that on that date Sita Ram was as- sessed at Rs. 1-14-0 as income-tax on Rs. 180 for the year 1931-32.

item.purpose: State the Additional Civil Judge's finding on the 'agriculturist' status and 'loan' definition under the 1940 Act.
item.relation_question: How did the executing court determine whether the applicants qualified as agriculturists and whether the transaction constituted a loan under the 1940 Act?
item.limit: Found Sita Ram was not assessed at the date of application or 1931 mortgage; held case covered by Act.

resolved_originals.text: By his judgment delivered on February 22, 1943, the Additional Civil Judge found that Sita Ram was not assessed to income-tax either at the date of the application under cite14†section 8 or at the date of the mortgage of 1931 and, there- fore, held that the applicants were agriculturists and that the case related to a loan as defined in Act XIII of 1940.

item.purpose: Explain the lower court's decision to reopen accounts from 1922 and declare the decree discharged.
item.relation_question: From what date did the Additional Civil Judge order accounts to be reopened, and what was the final financial conclusion regarding the debt?
item.limit: Relied on evidence from Suit No. 33 of 1938; noted non-production of books by decree-holders.

resolved_originals.text: He then went on to discuss the question whether the account should be reopened from June 2, 1922, when the earlier mortgage was executed or from July 28, 1931, when the mort- gage in suit was executed. The decree-holders who did not adduce any evidence on the hearing of the application evi- dently relied on the evidence adduced in suit No. 33 of 1938.

After discussing that evidence the learned Judge came to the conclusion that so far as the judgment-debtors were concerned the mortgagees in the two mortgages were one and the same. He adversely commented on the non-production of the books of account by the decree-holders.

Re-opening the accounts from June 2, 1922, the learned Judge concluded that the whole of the principal and interest payable accord- ing to the Act had been fully discharged and that nothing remained due by the judgmentdebtors under the decree in suit No. 33 of 1938. He 650 accordingly declared that the decree stood discharged in full and directed a note to that effect to be made in the Register of Suits.

item.purpose: Detail the High Court's reasoning for dismissing the decree-holders' appeal on the 'agriculturist' issue.
item.relation_question: Why did the High Court Division Bench hold that the question of Sita Ram's status in 1931 was immaterial?
item.limit: Applied Section 21 and Full Bench precedent (Ketki Kunwar v. Ram Saroop); focused on status at date of suit.

resolved_originals.text: The decree-holders having appealed to the High Court, a Division Bench (B. Mallik, C.J. and'Bind Basni Prasad J.) by its judgment delivered on April 16, 1948, held that the question whether Sita Ram was or was not an agriculturist on July 28, 1931, was not material as it was not denied that all the judgment, debtors were agriculturists on the date of suit.

Reference was made by the learned Judges to cite12†section 21 and it was stated that by reason of that section the mortgage amount could be recovered only from the mortgaged property and not personally from the mortgagors and accord- ingly the proviso to the definition of "loan" in cite13†section 2 (9) of the Act had no application and it was, therefore, not necessary to show that the borrowers were agriculturists at the date when the advance was made and that as the judgment-debtors were admittedly agriculturists at the date of the suit, the case was fully covered by the Full Bench decision of that High Court in Ketki Kunwar v.

Ram Saroop (1). The High Court, therefore, dismissed the appeal on this point alone. The question whether the account should be reopened from 1922 or from 1931 was not raised by the decree-holders at all. ]he decree-holders have now come up on appeal before us on a certificate granted by the High Court under cite18†section 110 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
